clue.text: Vehicle with favourite floor covering

parts.note: a car is the everyday vehicle
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a floor covering arrives with their favourite in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitted rug laid over a whole room is the standard floor covering.

clue.text: This may be seen in allotment, or in church bordering Scottish lake

definitions.text: This may be seen in allotment

indicators.note: the church abbreviation sits on either side of, so borders, the lake

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Gardening and Scottish scenery: something spotted on a vegetable plot or in a lakeside kirk.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic pointer: a bell-shaped glass cover protecting seedlings is a familiar sight on an allotment, a rented vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-shaped glass or plastic cover for young plants is typical equipment on a vegetable plot.

clue.text: Practised, as coffin put back in funeral carriage?

definitions.text: coffin put back in funeral carriage?
definitions.meaning: a coffin placed again in the hearse has been 'hearsed' a second time

explanation.surface: A grim image of undertakers drilling: the coffin keeps going back into the hearse.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-HEARSED: placed in the hearse again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play or speech is to practise it before the performance.

clue.text: Promotion for hearing device that cuts down noise

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a plug is a piece of publicity or promotion

explanation.surface: An advert promoting a hearing gadget that reduces noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft stopper worn in the ear canal blocks out sound, which is exactly a noise-reducing device.

clue.text: Make certain disc is about to be condemned

indicators.note: the disc goes about, or around, the phrase meaning make certain

parts.note: CD is a compact disc
to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Someone checking that a record is about to be banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'nearly' in 'is about to be'; it is really the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be censured is to be formally criticised or condemned.

clue.text: Consumes some of the contents of meatsafe

indicators.note: only part of the letters inside the word meatsafe are taken

explanation.surface: Someone helping themselves to food from a meat cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A meatsafe is a ventilated cupboard for storing meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumes, in the sense of food, simply means takes in as a meal.

clue.text: Stones 7″ perhaps captivates husband

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the record holds the husband inside

parts.note: a seven-inch vinyl record is a single

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones seven-inch record charms a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' suggests the band, and 7″ the record format; in fact 'Stones' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the mass of small rounded pebbles on a beach, so a collective word for stones.

clue.text: Bad weather, we hear, as a rule

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the next word is a sound-alike

parts.note: rain is the bad weather

explanation.surface: A grumble that wet weather is, as a rule, the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' reads like 'usually'; 'rule' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of their rule.

clue.text: Worn down — or marked down, in one's 27?

definitions.meaning: 27 across is end-of-course exams; being given a lower grade in them is to be ...

explanation.surface: A student feeling worn out, or marked down in their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, final examinations; the second reading is DE-GRADED, given a lower mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock or land that is degraded has been eroded, worn down over time.

clue.text: Parents not married? Not us

indicators.note: not means the married abbreviation is left out

parts.note: mothers are parents

explanation.surface: Unmarried parents, a social comment ending 'not us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Other people, everyone apart from ourselves, is what 'not us' means.

clue.text: Making mark but not voting; sailor leaves

indicators.note: the sailor leaves, so his letters are removed

parts.note: abstaining means declining to vote
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor departs having marked a ballot rather than voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Staining something leaves a mark or discoloration on it.

clue.text: News item resulting in furrowed brow?

definitions.meaning: the main title over a newspaper story
a crease across the forehead is a line on the head

explanation.surface: A shocking news story that makes the reader frown.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the answer literally: a wrinkle on the forehead is a line on one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The bold title over a newspaper story stands for the news item itself.

clue.text: Almost new before breakfast?

parts.note: anything before breakfast happens early in the day

explanation.surface: Something almost brand new, delivered just before breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly are synonyms, both meaning not quite.

clue.text: List stated a sexual identification

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: a gender is a person's identification as male, female or otherwise

explanation.surface: A form listing someone's declared gender identity.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'a gender' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Destroy the French, making a great commotion

parts.note: to bust something is to break or destroy it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Smashing up the French, causing a huge uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hustle and bustle is busy noisy activity, a commotion.

clue.text: Music to put one's name to?

definitions.text: Music to put one's name to?

parts.words: Music to put one's name to?
parts.note: a melody identifying a performer or show, read as tunes to which one signs one's name

explanation.surface: A puzzling request for music to sign one's name to.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting one's name to a document is signing it; the theme tune identifying a show or performer is the punning answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring theme played to identify a programme or entertainer, like an autograph in sound.

clue.text: Not very brave UN soldier, maybe, harbouring ill-will

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the ill-will goes inside

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, hence 'maybe'
gall is bitterness, ill-will

explanation.surface: A peacekeeping soldier who is cowardly and resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' looks military but is the ant, whose soldier caste guards the nest; 'harbouring' places the ill-will between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means brave, so its negative describes someone lacking courage or chivalry.

clue.text: Trimming hair somewhere underneath

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
below means in a place underneath

explanation.surface: A haircut, trimming somewhere low down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimming' looks like cutting hair; it is the noun for a decorative frill.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or ruffle, ornamental trimming on a dress.

clue.text: Where to look for vest?

parts.note: a vest, a British undershirt, belongs among garments worn beneath others

explanation.surface: Someone searching a drawer for a vest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat, so it is found among underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A British vest is a garment worn beneath the shirt, so it belongs with undergarments.

clue.text: Creature laying eggs on climbing grass

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the grass word reads upwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A bird or animal laying its eggs on grass that climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This small European deer is a wild creature of woods and fields.

clue.text: Pretend the writer's a machine with energy

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter; the writer is = I'm
a gin is a machine, as in cotton gin
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A writer posing as an energy-driven machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's' expands to 'the writer is', I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to make-believe, as children pretend in play.

clue.text: Peter's excited to be ready in advance

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter is so eager that he is ready early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges PETERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A preset control is adjusted beforehand, so set ready ahead of time.

clue.text: Continually bother this wild creature

definitions.meaning: the black-and-white burrowing animal of British woods

explanation.surface: A wild animal that keeps pestering.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag them persistently, from the old sport of baiting the animal.

clue.text: Garment making girl very warm in the middle

indicators.note: the warm word sits in the middle of the girl's name

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: A garment that keeps a girl very warm around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Where to buy new tree? Liar!

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where to get a new tree and is called a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TREELIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or seller dealing with the public is where customers make purchases.

clue.text: Star gundog ultimately turned up antelopes

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word gundog

explanation.surface: A prize gundog finally appears among antelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are a large African species of antelope.

clue.text: Unfinished business gents possibly deliver around the beginning of Easter

parts.note: a gents, a men's public lavatory, is one kind of loo

indicators.note: the deliver word wraps around the first letter of Easter

parts.note: to send is to deliver

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of Easter

explanation.surface: Tasks still to finish as Easter approaches, including fixing the gents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' is the British term for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail left unresolved, an outstanding piece of business.

clue.text: Last of tests?

parts.note: the closing exams of a degree course are the last tests a student sits

explanation.surface: A query about the last of the tests.
explanation.walkthrough: It also reads as last + S, the last of 'tests', though 'Last' cannot do both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: University students end their degrees with closing examinations, the last tests of all.

clue.text: She may serve 'sir' with a stew, carelessly

indicators.note: carelessly suggests a messy jumble of the letters

explanation.surface: A clumsy server slops stew on a customer addressed as sir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' rearranges SIR and A STEW together.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who brings food to tables in a restaurant serves diners.

clue.text: Clan uniting with alien group

parts.note: a sept is a branch of a clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A clan teams up with an extraterrestrial band.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-member band or ensemble is a group of musicians.
